status: RUN (2026-11-07). All 640 registered cells executed on the sixteen registered seeds; every gate passed and the frozen analysis path returned EXCLUSION PAYS AT SPARSE DENSITY AND GROWS WITH DENSITY.
question: At a fixed selection budget, does excluding the intra-cell row class buy precision on the world's edges in a sparse world, and how does that value move as the world densifies?

design.cells_arithmetic: 2 arms x 2 caps x 5 densities x 16 seeds = 320 judged cells in the primary scheme, and the same count again in the sensitivity scheme for the exposure check; 640 cells in total
design.world: 16 tags in four cells, |P_world| = 240 directed non-self pairs; W is a seed-and-density subset of the 192 cross-cell pairs, so no intra-cell row can ever be a world edge. The within-cell filler carries a FIXED event budget at every density (the constant family): it keeps the ineligible class competing for the ranking budget across the whole ladder, which is the Gate 13 condition the design record rests on. A1 used the proportional family, under which the filler's mass collapses as the world densifies and the dense end saturates
design.exposure: primary = fixed total exposure (400 events, 50 cycles at every density); sensitivity = fixed exposure per edge (each world edge emitted twice, so the horizon grows with |W|)
design.cap_note: precision at a fixed cap is the endpoint: its denominator is the arm's own selection. Coverage divides by |W|, which grows 24 to 192, so a coverage difference is forced by arithmetic

control.name: global count-ranked top-k
control.rule: rank every candidate row by count, ties on the engine's own key, take the top k

intra_cell_excluded.name: intra-cell-excluded ranking
intra_cell_excluded.rule: the same count ordering over the eligible rows only; rows whose two tags sit in one cell are not eligible

seeds.freshness: the first contiguous window of seventeen integers at or above 20330201 that appears in no file under docs, tests, benchmarks, research-journal or papers; the seventeenth is the bootstrap seed

criteria.estimand: Delta(rho) = precision(intra_cell_excluded, cap 20) - precision(control, cap 20) at density rho
criteria.C1: level at the sparse end on precision at the primary cap: mean over seeds of Delta(0.1) at or above the sparse bar, with its paired interval's lower bound above zero and at least eleven of sixteen seeds positive
criteria.C2: the interaction Delta(0.8) - Delta(0.1) is NOT a criterion. It is reported with its interval and its per-seed values, because the dense end is pinned by the pool's composition (the pilot measured Delta(0.8) = 0.150 with zero spread on eight seeds), so a criterion there would be arithmetic rather than evidence
criteria.bar_provenance: calibrated on eight UNREGISTERED seeds (992001-992008) before this block existed, where the sparse-end mean was 0.094 with a per-seed sd of 0.062; the bar is set at roughly half that mean so the block is powered (~0.8 at sixteen seeds) rather than fitted to the judged run. Rule 19 permits calibration only on data that is not being judged, and these seeds are not in the block
criteria.exposure_rule: if the sparse-end level does not hold under the sensitivity scheme, the verdict is EXPOSURE ARTIFACT and nothing is adopted
criteria.judged_whole: C1 is the whole judged criterion; the gates are preconditions, not scores, and the density slope is a description rather than a second criterion

rules.G0 liveness: the two arms' selected sets must differ on at least fourteen of sixteen seeds at the sparse end in the primary scheme
rules.G1 presence ceiling: every world edge must be present in the pool at every cell (presence = 1.0)
rules.G2 arithmetic: covered cannot exceed asserted; precision must equal covered over asserted; precision cannot exceed 1; rho_rank is reported for every cell
rules.G3 axis live: rho_rank must rise from the sparsest to the densest level in both schemes
rules.G4 control reproduces Gate 13: the control's mean precision at the sparse end must not exceed 0.50
rules.G5 identity where it must hold: on a pool whose every row is a world edge, the two arms must select the same set and Delta must be exactly 0
rules.G6 treatment does what it claims: coverage of the treatment must be at least the control's on every cell

gates.void_rule: a failed gate voids the block and no criterion is read; a cell set that is not the pre-registered grid is refused

decision_table.condition: gates pass; C1 passes; the interaction interval lies above zero
decision_table.verdict: EXCLUSION PAYS AT SPARSE DENSITY AND GROWS WITH DENSITY
decision_table.reading: the freed budget buys more as the world's edge set grows; this is the A1 mechanism, now measured where the treatment is not pinned
decision_table.decision: adopt intra-cell exclusion as an allocation change behind a recorded owner decision; no behavioural claim

decision_table.condition: gates pass; C1 passes; the interaction interval straddles zero
decision_table.verdict: EXCLUSION PAYS AT SPARSE DENSITY; DENSITY SLOPE NOT IDENTIFIED
decision_table.reading: the exclusion buys precision where the world is sparse, and the block cannot place how that changes with density
decision_table.decision: adopt at the sparse end; move the density question to the candidate space, since the dense end is pinned by composition

decision_table.condition: gates pass; C1 passes; the interaction interval lies below zero
decision_table.verdict: EXCLUSION PAYS MORE AT SPARSE THAN DENSE
decision_table.reading: the crowded class, not density, is the lever; the dense end has little left to fix
decision_table.decision: adopt at the sparse end; retire the density interaction as a moderator of this bottleneck

decision_table.verdict: EXCLUSION DOES NOT PAY AT SPARSE DENSITY
decision_table.reading: removing the ineligible class does not buy precision at the budget where Gate 13's observation lives
decision_table.decision: retire budget competition as the lever at this cap and world family; move the line to the candidate space

decision_table.condition: gates pass; a criterion passes but the sensitivity scheme's sparse-end mean is not positive
decision_table.reading: the direction reverses under the other exposure scheme

decision_table.condition: gates pass; a criterion fails and the interval is wider than 0.30
decision_table.reading: the interval cannot place the sparse-end level; absence is not established
decision_table.decision: neither pole; a new block on fresh seeds may be registered, never a re-read

decision_table.reading: reported as the gate, never as a verdict

analysis.runner_note: the out path is named because the module's default is A1's artifact; a pre-run fix, disclosed before the first cell

pilot.why: calibration on unregistered seeds: the block's seeds are not measured here, and these seeds are not in the block
pilot.dense_end_is_pinned: at cap 20 the dense pool holds 192 world rows and 48 intra rows, so the control's top 20 is 17 world rows and the treatment's is 20: Delta(0.8) = 0.150 with no spread on any seed. That is why the interaction cannot be a criterion
pilot.power: for the sparse bar 0.05 at sixteen seeds the standard error is 0.0155 and the power against the pilot mean 0.094 is about 0.8

not_evidence: no behavioural claim: the endpoint is the share of a fixed budget spent on world edges
one world family, one vocabulary and one filler family; the proportional filler family is A1, which is held and unrun
the pilot is calibration on unregistered seeds, not a result about the hypothesis
a pass licenses an allocation change on this layer only, behind a recorded decision

leverage_audit.endpoint: precision at a fixed cap; the denominator is the arm's own selection

run.verdict: EXCLUSION PAYS AT SPARSE DENSITY AND GROWS WITH DENSITY
run.read_once: the analysis path ran once, as frozen; no criterion was re-read after the result was seen
